extracted.intended_audience: PhD students and early-career researchers considering peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for PhD students on whether and how to accept manuscript review invitations, weighing benefits (skill development, career/networking, service) against risks (lack of expertise, time cost), with concrete timing and volume recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill development
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing sharpens critical analysis; 'Reviewing manuscripts requires more concentration and attention to detail' than casual reading and helps you spot methodological issues in your own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviewing as training: it improves manuscript-reading rigor and helps you identify methodological flaws you might otherwise miss in your own research. Treat reviews as deliberate practice in critique and methods evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career building
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing strengthens academic job applications and demonstrates 'versatility, critical analysis skills, and a selfless attitude to supporting the research community.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reviewing activity on CVs and job materials to evidence scholarly service and professional competencies. Consider reviews as part of your academic profile and networking narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing connects you with journal editors and academics in your field, which can open doors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting reviews strategically can build relationships with editors and senior researchers; target requests to journals and areas where you want to increase visibility and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributing to the field (service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing supports research-community integrity by contributing peer evaluation and quality control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View peer review as community service that sustains research standards. Balance altruism with personal costs; participation helps maintain the scholarly ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing / expertise concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Early-stage doctoral students may lack sufficient expertise to provide high-quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about accepting reviews in your first year(s); consider waiting until you have substantive domain knowledge. If unsure, decline or consult your supervisor before accepting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time investment / unpaid work
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing is unpaid work that can compete with your own research and writing commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh review invitations against current project deadlines and workload. Prioritize tasks that advance your PhD; decline when reviewing would meaningfully delay your progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation — wait 12+ months before volunteering
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific advice to wait 12+ months into your PhD before volunteering to review manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the first year to build foundational knowledge and confidence; after ~12 months you'll be better positioned to assess others' work. This is a suggested minimum—adjust based on your background and field norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation — review sparingly (one paper per publication you produce)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline to limit reviewing roughly to one paper for each paper you publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this as a heuristic to avoid overcommitting; align review volume with your own research productivity so service doesn't impede output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation — strategically target journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice to focus reviewing efforts on journals where you want to build connections and visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept assignments from journals relevant to your research program or career goals. Strategic selection maximizes networking benefits and time ROI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation — balance unpaid duty with PhD priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit guidance to balance the duty of reviewing against priority PhD tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize thesis milestones, grant deadlines, and publication timelines over reviewing when conflicts arise. Use selective acceptance, negotiations on deadlines, or co-reviewing with supervisors to mitigate burden.
